A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same trace-rewriting study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original teacher/student accuracy and watermark-detection experiments, including appendix ablations, additional benchmarks, and adaptive-distillation tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds trace-quality measurements, adaptive-distillation comparisons, answer-only distillation, and model-size analyses.

M1.justification: The semantic and optimized prompts, gradient-based variants, HotFlip procedure, and watermark insertion method are retained. The added attacks and model-size experiments evaluate the existing proposed methods rather than change them.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K/GSM8K-Platinum, MATH, MMLU, and MMLU-Pro. The additions reuse these datasets and downstream tasks; they vary distillation procedures, model configurations, or measurements rather than introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands the adaptive comparisons by evaluating KPOD against anti-distillation and CDG-KD against watermarking in Figures 5–7. Table 4 also introduces an answer-only comparator. ADS, DOGe, and the four existing watermarking baselines remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include perplexity and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite judgments on 150 MATH traces, adaptive and answer-only distillation procedures, and varied teacher/rewriter configurations. The original dataset splits, standard SFT budget, and principal accuracy/detection metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of trace quality, resistance to KPOD and CDG-KD, removal of reasoning supervision, and dependence on teacher/rewriter size. The Direct ablation and paraphrasing/filtering tests already existed in v1; their relocation alone is not an addition.

E5.justification: New Table 2 reports mean perplexity with standard deviations across 150 traces. This adds sample-variability reporting, not evidence of repeated training runs. Both versions retain the 100 independent trials per query budget for watermark detection.

E6.justification: The retained headline comparisons in Figures 2–3 and Table 1 are unchanged, but substantial results are added in Figures 5–7 and Tables 2–5. Examples include quality scores of 3.83 for OPT versus 4.01 for original traces, answer-only accuracies, and a 27.5-point student accuracy reduction with a 7B teacher and 7B rewriter.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, rewriting constraints, prompt-scoring expression, and gradient/HotFlip derivations are retained. The single-source assumption emphasized in v2 was already present in v1. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: anti-distillation while preserving teacher utility, and reliable watermark detection with nearly zero false alarms. The headline 61.3-point student accuracy reduction is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving rewriter error correction, degenerate repetition behind low baseline perplexity, and CDG-KD's mismatch with behavioral watermarks. Its answer-only interpretation is overstated: Table 4 shows one improvement over OPT, 6.5% versus 5.3% for Llama-3.2-1B on MATH. The main limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository URL in the abstract and identifies the reference, judge, and additional models used in the new analyses. Existing prompts, optimization settings, LoRA hyperparameters, preprocessing, and hardware disclosures are retained. Repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds Feng et al. (2024) and Yi et al. (2025) for the evaluated adaptive methods, plus Hsieh et al. (2023) and Chen et al. (2025) for answer-only interpretation. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Related Work becomes a standalone section, appendix robustness material is consolidated into Section 6.4, and new analysis subsections and acknowledgments are added. There are localized wording and author-line edits, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 changes typography throughout, adds four tables, and relocates and expands v1 Figures 9, 14, and 15 into main-text Figures 5–7 with new attack series and revised legends/captions. The resulting display reorganization is substantial; other retained figures are principally renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for central requirements that v1 evaluated incompletely: preserving trace quality and resisting adaptive distillation. Appendix B directly measures quality, Section 6.4 tests additional adaptive methods, and Table 5 establishes effectiveness beyond the original 7B-teacher/120B-rewriter pairing. These gains outweigh the limited overstatement of answer-only results, although that interpretation should acknowledge Table 4's exception.
